utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have two questions to raise, Judges. The first question is: I should like to remind you that the Trial Chamber is inter alia competent or, rather, in charge of monitoring the health condition and the detention conditions of the accused. Generally, the conditions of detention are systematically deteriorating for all the convicts, and the culmination was a couple of days ago. For over ten years, the convicts, as you know, are entitled to two walks a day, one an hour's and another one for 45 minutes. For over ten years, these walks had been organised in the courtyard by the building itself, by the prison building itself, from which one can see lots of trees and where there are two grass lawns where the grass is always green. A few days ago, a tunnel was constructed through this courtyard. We were prohibited to walk in that courtyard, and they lead us into a courtyard where one cannot at all see any trees, where there is no grass at all, where we have concrete surrounding us from five sides, the left side, the right side, down from the bottom, north, south, east and west, and the floor is concrete. We do see the sky, in all fairness, but the sun doesn't reach us. This has terribly affected, for the worst, the mood of all the convicts, by 30 per cent, I should say. This is in contravention of any standards that have to be ensured for convicts, for detainees, in the world, in the civilised world. We have to see the sun when it is sunny and we have to have greenery where we take our walks. This has been completely abolished. Different things are now happening in the prison. There have been ideas that we should collectively boycott the walk, but we are unable to reach an agreement. You know, convicts are divided amongst themselves into those who think that they should curry favour with the administration and the Registry and those who are a bit more rebellious, a bit more resolved, so that collective action is regrettably impossible. Perhaps that is because we are not true criminals, but high political leaders and police officials; and that is why we are unable to reach agreement. I think that this problem has to be solved and that you, as the Trial Chamber, on the basis of this individual grievance, should actually intervene with the President of the Court for the restitution of the old conditions for the walks. For the sake of the health of convicts, the conditions in which we have our daily walks and the duration of those walks is much more important than anything else. It is much more important than our daily food, and this is something that we learned in our penology textbooks, and we learned this in our third year of studies. The second question which I wanted to raise is this: You know well that I was given, on the 29th of September, the decision of the Registrar that I would be no longer allowed to use the privileged telephone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With respect to the first matter you've raised, we're going to make some inquiries. I, myself, had no ideas that these two walks of one hour and 45 minutes were taking place in a space with grass and trees in the past and that you now find yourself in a space with only concrete around you because some tunnel, supposedly, was built. I suppose this tunnel was built or dug by the prison authorities and not by detainees, but we'll make some inquiries. Obviously, it's good for morale to be able to see the sun. We'll make some inquiries. Okay, tell us about this second matter.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, just an additional piece of information. This tunnel was constructed for a purpose out of prefabricated elements. A wall was punched to enable us access to this new courtyard, where there are no conditions. So the tunnel is exclusively there for that purpose, to enable us to pass through this courtyard so that when we walk to the courtyard where we are going to take our walks, we cannot see the sun. The second question is this: You know that on the 29th of September, the Registrar handed me a written decision prohibiting me from using the so-called privileged telephone. This decision had a deadline of 30 days of application. The 29th of September was the first day of its application. It was that day on which I was prohibited to further use that telephone. The decision expired yesterday. The working hours of the Registrar ended today at 1730. I have not received another or a new decision, nor have I had any information, so I don't know what happens now. It had always been the practice for information about the expiry of a specific measure to be given to the person concerned, but in the contrary case, I should have received a paper with the number of telephone of my legal adviser which I could show to the guards so that they would make it possible for me to use that telephone, because I do not do the dialing myself, the guards do, and only that particular number which is on that piece of paper. So this is yet another violation of his official duty on the part of the Registrar. I cannot qualify it otherwise. This is what I had to say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I'm sure the Registry will inform us, based on the Rules. Should there be a new tapping device for 30 days, you should be informed of it, as per the Rules. It may be that you are being advised, because you're sitting here in this courtroom this afternoon and you might be informed later on, but I know nothing about this. There again, I know that the Registry checks the transcript second by second. I'm sure the Registry's aware that you have raised these two issues, that inevitably the Judges will be informed. With regard to next week, Mr. Seselj, for the time being, and I'm saying "for the time being" because you never know, there are always unforeseen things happening, we have VS-1017 [as interpreted] - I won't mention the name because this is a protected witness - and we have Ms. Bosanac, a 92 ter witness, and VS-1131. Is there anything new, Ms. Dahl?

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. With respect, I'd like to correct the pseudonym that appears on the transcript. The witness for Tuesday is VS-17. If he doesn't appear, we'll proceed to Dr. Bosanac. On Wednesday, we will hear from VS-1131; and on Thursday, a new addition to the schedule to try to ensure the timely use of the courtroom, VS-1119.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] VS-1119, is that a 92 ter or a viva voce witness? I can't remember, Ms. Dahl.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's a 92 ter witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Seselj, we have possibly four witnesses scheduled, VS-17, Ms. Bosanac, VS-1131, and VS-1119, it being understood that the last three are 92 ter witnesses.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, over these past two months I haven't been informed about this witness at all, VS-1119. I'm looking through my papers right now. I can't find him yet. I don't have him on this schedule at all, on the list for the period until mid-December. So this is quite a surprise. I don't know who this is and I don't know whether I'll be in a position to prepare for that witness. I simply cannot recall that this witness was mentioned at all, 1119. Oh, yes, I know who that is, but that's also a 92 ter witness. Now I know who that witness is. You see, in respect of next week, 017 is the only one who's testifying viva voce, and the Prosecutor's not sure whether this person will come. You know that this is a contentious witness, because this witness said that he would be a Defence witness. I have no contact with this person, so I really don't know anything, I really don't know anything. All the others are 92 ter witnesses. You can finish three 92 ter witnesses within one session, an hour and a half, because you know I'm not going to examine them -- cross-examine them. So the Prosecutor is, in this way, letting us know that they haven't got enough material for next week either. We lost time last week, the week before that, this week one day. I don't mind, because my throat is not very well, but this is wrong on the part of the Prosecution, this manner of handling things is wrong.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, in principle, we should have, at most, four witnesses or at least three for sure. That's obvious. And we have a schedule for the week after next. The Trial Chamber is having a very close look at all this in order to ascertain which are the remaining witnesses, to see whether the Trial Chamber is to hand down rulings in this respect, so we're working on it. Of course, our main concern is to avoid any gap in the scheduling, is to do our level best for all the witnesses to come. Whilst we are at it, Mr. Seselj, I had told you that the Trial Chamber could reconvene after the recess as of the week before the 12th of January, 2009, as early as on the 9th of January, back then. Regarding the Tuesday, that's the -- Wednesday, that's the Orthodox new year, if I'm not mistaken. You didn't want to have any hearing on that day, and I said it was not a problem, we could sit on the Tuesday, the Thursday and the Friday. But after thinking it over, I thought that it's likely that there's not going to be any hearings on Thursday and Friday, because other Trial Chambers would not have resumed yet. It might be better to sit on Thursday, say from 9.00 to 12.30 and from 2.30 to 5.00, and on Friday we could do the same, so have a morning session and then work until 4.00 or 4.30, so that in two days we would have worked as much as if we'd been sitting for three days. Is there any inconvenience for you there?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, if that is going to be an exception only that week, I agree. But you know of my problems with my spine. It's not like I asked for breaks like some witnesses here. However, it is a permanent problem, and when I wait for two hours here, it's in a cell, it's in an uncomfortable chair, and I cannot recline at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If ever during a hearing you were to experience back problems, if you would like us to stop, to have a break, do say so immediately. So far, personally, I thought that you didn't have any problem, but I raised the issue during the pre-trial phase and you said that you were really firing on all cylinders, that there was no problem at all. So maybe you need to walk about a little, as it were, and if you need to just have a stretch, just say so. We can have a 15-minute break. Of course, the Trial Chamber will accommodate you, no problem at all.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would just like to remind you that I had three reasons when I asked to sit for only three days a week. The first reason was the fact that I represent myself, and bearing in mind the experience of the Milosevic case. The second reason was asthma, and the third reason was problems with my spine. I've already had spine surgery once. Those were the three reasons I asked for the sittings only three days a week, and you accepted that. You understood those reasons, as a Pre-Trial Judge back in those days, even. However, if it is only going to be two days, if it is now going to be a precedent that is going to be repeated later on, I don't mind; I could take it for two days. I would have a problem if that were to become regular practice afterwards.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No problem whatsoever. I'm now addressing the Prosecution. Do you have any other matters?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Have we gone through all your issues, Mr. Seselj? If that is so, we shall adjourn to reconvene on Tuesday in the morning, I believe, at 8.30. Thank you. The hearing stands adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 4th day of November, 2008, at 8.30 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 6.25 p.m.,
